newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN refugee chief slams Gabon expulsion of Rwandans.
newsitem.headline: UN refugee chief slams Gabon expulsion of Rwandans.

text.p: The head of the U.N. refugee agency condemned Gabon on Tuesday for forcibly sending home eight Rwandan Hutus recognised as refugees among 168 flown out in a predawn military operation.
Sadako Ogata also expressed concern that other asylum countries in central Africa should allow her staff time to separate the "innocent who deserve protection" from genocide perpetrators.

In a statement, the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said it had found seven of the eight among 45 returnees being held in a transit centre in Kigali. Most of the 45 were women or children separated from men upon arrival.
"We strongly condemn the Gabonese government's action in forcing these eight back," Ogata was quoted as saying.
"Such conduct by Gabon, which is a signatory to international conventions on the treatment of refugees, is a flagrant violation of the most basic human rights and humanitarian principles," she added.

But the UNHCR expressed concern over 123 mostly male refugees who were handcuffed and taken to an undisclosed destination upon arrival. It was working with the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to locate them.
Gabon expelled to Rwanda the last 168 refugees and fugitives who fled there among 1,300 who came last month.
They had trekked for months across the former Zaire and later fled fierce fighting in the Congo to arrive in Gabon, which is 1,600 km (1,000 miles) west of Rwanda.

"There are several thousand Rwandans scattered in countries across central Africa," Ogata said. "It is vital that asylum countries allow us time to separate the innocent who deserve protection. These people need our help."

Earlier, spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole told a news briefing that Gabon had acted before UNHCR could finish its assessments to distinguish innocent refugees from fugitive participants in Rwanda's 1994 genocide.

Among those sent home were 43 soldiers of the former Rwandan government army and some civilians who had admitted having taken part in an attempted hijacking during an aborted attempt to send them home from Gabon last Saturday.
The Rwandans being screened by UNHCR to determine their status in recent weeks included about 100 whom the Gabonese government said had volunteered to go home.

Last Friday, UNHCR announced it had begun cooperating with a U.N. war crimes tribunal hunting ringleaders of Rwanda's 1994 genocide. The agency said it was assisting investigators from the Arusha-based tribunal investigating the Hutu-led slaughter of more than half a million minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus.

A large proportion of those who reached Gabon were soldiers of the former Rwandan army, which played a key role in the genocide, and included high-ranking ex-officers. A Tutsi-dominated government took power in Kigali after the Hutu administration collapsed.
